title: A child that serves several requesters is stopped when the last requester leaves, and never before
description: A shared child (one cargo build, one broker) runs in its own process group, outside the group of every requester, so stopping a requester's own task cannot reach it. The registry counts requesters per key: acquiring with a key that has a running child adds the requester (a requester counts once however often it acquires) and starts nothing; releasing removes the requester (a second release of the same lease does nothing); the release that leaves no requester takes the child out of the registry at once (a later acquire starts a fresh child) and stops its process tree gracefully through the termination law, with the signal recorded. A child that ended by itself is dropped at the next acquire. A requester that ends releases every key it holds with `releaseAll`.
